workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
rationale: The registered one-bit-per-source-edge Gray premise and unbranched two-stage receiver establish a good logical topology, but the contract explicitly declines reset/startup and receiver inter-bit timing premises while exposing wr_seen to pointer comparison. Pointer-consumer safety and whole-IP/FIFO acceptance are therefore unknown, not good. Fit only as a scoped unknown boundary/integration case, never a clean FIFO control.
caveats: Unlike C03 there is no startup ignore guarantee. Obtain startup comparison gating/initialization, receiver bit-skew bounds preventing overlap of successive source transitions, and physical metastability closure. Whole FIFO additionally needs memory/collision, full/empty and wrap policy; do not invent those implementations. Independent Icarus run of the supplied bench passes with final value 8. Reproduce: iverilog -g2012 -s bench -o /tmp/c09-settle C09/case.sv C09/bench.sv; vvp /tmp/c09-settle. Bench loop i=1;i<16 checks 15 transitions from initialized 0000 through Gray(15)=1000, not the wrap to Gray(0); it does not check consumed pointer decisions or any FIFO. A claim of a complete cyclic sequence is overstated.

author_reading.proposed_outcome: Positive Gray-pointer synchronizer premise control; whole FIFO remains unqualified
author_reading.evidence_and_limits: Bench checks one-bit changes over a complete modulo-16 Gray sequence. Verify RTL producer really maintains the stated Gray contract. Need full/empty/reset/collision review, physical bus-skew bounds, synchronizer placement/MTBF.

labels.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
labels.rationale: The site has the standard two-stage registered Gray-pointer topology under the explicit one-bit-per-source-edge premise. No definite logical crossing defect is shown. However no reset/startup consumption contract or inter-bit timing bound is asserted, so unconditional safety at the pointer consumer or whole FIFO is not established.
labels.caveats: Close pointer safety by specifying initialized pointer values and ignoring wr_seen until synchronization is established, plus a reviewed inter-bit skew/max-delay bound preventing overlap of successive source transitions at g1 and metastability closure. Close full FIFO acceptance separately with memory collision semantics and full/empty/wrap correctness evidence. Supplied Gray bench passes but proves only its deterministic sequence, not these facts. Fit as an unknown pointer fragment, not a whole-IP known-good FIFO control.

labels.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
labels.rationale: Site-level structural control only: contract line 7 guarantees a registered Gray pointer changing at most one bit per source edge, and line 5 supplies two stages with no intermediate consumer. With physical skew closure, sampling a transition yields an adjacent old/new Gray value. No unrelated data crossing exists in the shown module.
labels.caveats: Not fit as a whole-FIFO good qualification control: reset/startup, memory collisions, full/empty correctness and physical inter-bit skew are explicitly unasserted. verdict good applies only to the stated pointer structure, not these absent facts. Supplied bench passes but exercises only 15 non-wrap transitions and establishes neither FIFO correctness nor skew. Missing physical skew can invalidate the Gray premise at receiver pins; RTL alone cannot close it.
